message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible public vulnerability reports and material updates observed in the 24-hour window before the scheduled run on 2026-07-22 at 05:10 IST. Fresh, relevant findings were found for Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Ubuntu, OpenSSH on Ubuntu, and WordPress. A few items, including 7-Zip CVE-2026-14266, were excluded because the primary disclosure date was outside the 24-hour window.

**Finding 1: Google Chrome desktop security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: 12 security fixes, including CVE-2026-16420 through CVE-2026-16424 and related high-severity Chromium issues.
- Severity: High for the externally highlighted CVEs listed by Google.
- Description: Google released Chrome Stable 150.0.7871.181/.182 for Windows and Mac and 150.0.7871.181 for Linux, addressing multiple browser flaws including type confusion, input validation, buffer overflow, use-after-free, and GPU/UI issues.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Google Chrome, and Google's release explicitly applies to Chrome desktop on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases, 2026-07-21: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/07/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_0256605430.html

**Finding 2: Mozilla Firefox 153 security advisory**

- Product: Mozilla Firefox
- Issue: MFSA 2026-68, covering many CVEs including CVE-2026-16349, CVE-2026-16350, CVE-2026-16351, CVE-2026-16352, CVE-2026-16362, and additional high/moderate/low issues.
- Severity: Overall impact High, according to Mozilla.
- Description: Mozilla announced Firefox 153 with fixes for same-origin policy bypass, use-after-free, sandbox escape, JIT/WebAssembly, graphics, networking, and other browser security issues.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Mozilla Firefox, and Mozilla's advisory explicitly names Firefox 153 as the fixed release.
- Source: Mozilla Foundation Security Advisory 2026-68: https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-68/

**Finding 3: Ubuntu security notice roll-up for July 21**

- Product: Ubuntu
- Issue: Multiple Ubuntu Security Notices, including USN-8582-1 for jbig2dec, USN-8581-1 for libarchive, USN-8580-1/2 for AccountsService, USN-8579-1 for snapd, and USN-8574-1 through USN-8576-1 for Linux kernel packages.
- Severity: Not clearly stated as a single overall severity by Canonical in the notices reviewed.
- Description: Canonical published several Ubuntu package updates on 2026-07-21 addressing vulnerabilities in image/PDF parsing, archive handling, local privilege-related desktop services, snapd, and multiple Linux kernel variants.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and the notices are first-party Canonical security notices for maintained Ubuntu releases.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices index, 2026-07-21 entries: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Finding 4: OpenSSH vulnerability fixed for Ubuntu 16.04 ESM**

- Product: OpenSSH / Ubuntu OpenSSH package
- Issue: CVE-2026-35414
- Severity: Not clearly stated by Canonical in the index entry reviewed.
- Description: Canonical published USN-8577-1 for an OpenSSH issue that could allow unintended access to network services.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes OpenSSH and Ubuntu. The notice is limited in the reviewed source to Ubuntu 16.04 LTS/ESM, so environments should confirm whether that legacy release is present before prioritizing.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices index, USN-8577-1 entry: https://ubuntu.com/security/notices

**Finding 5: WordPress wp2shell exploitation activity update**

- Product: WordPress
- Issue: WP2Shell chain involving CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137
- Severity: Critical/high depending on source and component; Rapid7 notes the GitHub advisory classifies CVE-2026-63030 as Critical while the current CVSS score cited there is 7.5.
- Description: The vulnerabilities were initially disclosed on 2026-07-17, but ELLIO published a 2026-07-21 threat report describing mass exploitation activity observed between July 18 and July 21 against WordPress targets.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes WordPress, and the fresh report is a material exploitation update for a WordPress Core vulnerability chain.
- Source: ELLIO threat report, 2026-07-21: https://ellio.tech/en/blog/wp2shell-in-the-wild-under-48-hours-from-patch-to-mass-exploitation/ ; Rapid7 technical summary: https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-63030-wp2shell-a-critical-remote-code-execution-vulnerability-in-wordpress-core/

**Possible matches needing review**

- Microsoft Windows WMI Providers: ZDI listed CVE-2026-50297 and CVE-2026-50325 on 2026-07-21 as Microsoft Windows local privilege escalation issues with CVSS 7.0. Products.txt includes Windows 10 and Windows Server 2012 R2, but the reviewed ZDI listing did not confirm exact affected Windows editions, so this should be checked against MSRC/NVD before operational prioritization. Source: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/published/

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for Chrome and Firefox desktop update coverage and for internet-facing WordPress sites because the WordPress item reflects active exploitation reporting. Ubuntu estates should review the July 21 Canonical notices according to installed packages and kernel variants. No fresh, clearly product-matched advisories were verified in this run for the remaining monitored products.
